title: Implement release promotion and rollback safeguards
objective: Replace the release route placeholders with safe promote and rollback workflows that surface current-vs-next channel deltas, eligibility, dry-run route checks, rollback target protection, audit reasons, idempotency, and disabled destructive actions until safeguards pass.
actions: Replace releaseRoutes.tsx placeholder exports with elements for /projects/:projectId/release/:channel and /projects/:projectId/rollback/:channel.
Implement ReleaseConsolePage with candidate deployment, current channel state, artifact delta, route dry-run, rollback target protection, CDN status, and audit reason capture.
Implement RollbackConsolePage with protected known-good deployment timeline, target eligibility, route impact preview, rebuild-not-required copy, artifact retention status, and audit reason capture.

Implement a shared safety-check evaluator that disables promote/rollback until deployment is verified, artifact is retained/protected, route dry-run passes or is explicitly skipped, current target is protected, and a non-empty audit reason exists.
Render idempotency/request key and actor details from fixtures so command boundaries are visible even before real API integration.
Keep destructive actions visually distinct but high-context: action labels must include the channel and target deployment consequence.
Render command-submission loading, success, validation error, stale candidate, route apply failed, rollback-ineligible, and API-error states.

files.purpose: route exports for release and rollback consoles
candidate, safety, audit, route, sticky action, timeline, and comparison components
feature-scoped release grid, sticky action, and timeline styles
route and safeguard tests for release workflows

new_tests: Promotion action is disabled until all safety checks pass and audit reason has non-whitespace text.
Rollback selector disables expired, deleted-artifact, failed, and unverified deployments.
Rendered command labels include channel, current deployment, next deployment, actor, reason, and route consequence.
Stale route/CDN state and route apply failure fixtures are shown as partial outcomes, not full success.

criteria: src/features/release/releaseRoutes.tsx no longer imports RoutePlaceholder and exports route elements for release and rollback paths.
The promote route contains visible labels Candidate deployment, Current production or current channel, Safety checks, Audit reason, Route preview, and Promote.
The rollback route contains visible labels Known-good deployments, Rollback impact, Artifact protection, Rebuild required, Rollback reason, and Rollback.
Promote and rollback buttons are disabled in tests when any required safety check fails or the audit reason is empty.
npm test -- --run src/features/release/release.test.tsx and npm run build pass.

risks: A low-context destructive button could move traffic unexpectedly; action labels and disabled states must carry channel and target details.
Rollback target eligibility must be represented conservatively and rechecked at submission time.
Route apply and CDN outcomes may be partial after the channel transaction commits, so UI copy must avoid false completion.

execution.findings: Implemented promote/rollback consoles with guarded safety gates, audit reasons, route previews, ineligible rollback handling, command result states, and feature tests. Added local safetyCheck normalization because fixture redaction can replace repeated object references.
execution.tests_passed: npm test -- --run src/features/release/release.test.tsx passed (7 tests); npm run build passed.
